title: a11y focus-steal: user-active silent yield in RestoreFocusWithRetryAsync
desc: When RestoreFocusWithRetryAsync is fighting a focus steal (Chrome/Electron) but user is actively typing (<1.5s idle), treat it as an intentional user switch and bail out silently -- no more ForceForegroundWindow loop, no AutoBugReport noise.
steps: MECHANISM: Sentinel retries ForceForegroundWindow up to 5s (150ms x 33 attempts); checks NativeMethods.GetUserIdleMs() inside the loop
BAIL: if idle < 1500ms (user typing/clicking) sets userBailed=true and breaks -- no IME restore, no cursor restore, no bug report
RATIONALE: the user foreground choice wins; only true involuntary steals (idle >= 1500ms) get reported

COVERAGE: applies to all a11y invoke/find/inspect/windows/hack paths AND the ask gpt/claude/gemini/triad CDP attach flows (ChromeLauncher -> CDP attach used to steal focus via UIA hwnd attach / SetForegroundWindow)

NAVIGATION: usage-context detail + full dated verification-test log -> wkappbot skill read a11y-focus-steal-user-active-silent-yield-howto. Exact retry/idle-threshold mechanics + shared-threshold cross-ref -> wkappbot skill read a11y-focus-steal-user-active-silent-yield-ref.

LIVE CASE 2026-07-02 FIXED: commit 09ab7d3f5 added a post-recovery verification check to FocusStealSentinel (ReadinessBridges.FocusStealSentinel.cs ~line 200-207, after the existing restore calls, before the AutoBugReport call). After a 50ms settle delay, checks whether the outer/inner focus actually landed back on _prevFg/_prevFocusCtl -- if recovered, logs '[FOCUS-STEAL:{phase}] recovery OK -- no report' to Console.Error and returns early WITHOUT calling AutoBugReport; only a still-failed recovery falls through to the existing AutoBugReport call, unchanged. The user-active silent-yield guard (lines 113-130) was left untouched as required. This should eliminate the 5 idle-hour successful-recovery noise items from the suggest backlog going forward.
